### 1. Medication absorption (transformed)

$X$ has pdf $f_X(x) = 3x^2$ and CDF $F_X(x) = x^3$ for $0 \leq x \leq 1$.

#### Part a

Let $Y = 100X$. Is this linear or nonlinear? What are the possible values of $Y$? Find $P(Y \leq 50)$ exactly.

::: answer
Linear, with $0 \leq Y \leq 100$. $P(Y \leq 50) = P(X \leq 0.5) = 0.5^3 = 0.125$
:::

#### Part b

Let $W = -\ln(X)$. Is this linear or nonlinear? What are the possible values of $W$? Find $P(W \leq 0.5)$ exactly.

::: answer
Not given
:::

#### Part c

Use the simulation method (simulate, transform, summarize) to check your answers to Parts a and b.

::: answer
```{r}
#| label: "q1c-simulate"
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3.5

set.seed(1616)
reps <- 10000
x_grid <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 10001)

dose_sims <- tibble(sim = 1:reps) |>
  mutate(x = sample(x_grid, size = n(), replace = TRUE,
                    prob = 3 * x_grid^2),
         y = 100 * x,
         w = -log(x))

prob_y <- mean(dose_sims$y <= 50)
```

$P(Y \leq 50) \approx$ `r round(prob_y, 4)`

Answers will vary slightly, but should be close to your answers in Parts a and b.
:::

#### Part d

Make a histogram of each of the simulated `x`, `y`, and `w` values. Which transformation kept the shape, and which changed it?

::: answer
```{r}
#| label: "q1d-histograms"
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3.5

ggplot(dose_sims, aes(x = y)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)),
                 binwidth = 2, boundary = 0,
                 color = "black", fill = "lightblue") +
  labs(title = "Simulated Y = 100X", x = "y", y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

ggplot(dose_sims, aes(x = w)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)),
                 binwidth = 0.1, boundary = 0,
                 color = "black", fill = "#E89543") +
  labs(title = "Simulated W = -ln(X)", x = "w", y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

$Y = 100X$ (linear) keeps the shape of $X$, just stretched to 0–100. $W = -\ln(X)$ (nonlinear) changes the shape: it piles up near 0 and has a long right tail.
:::

#### Part e

Add the pdf of an $\text{Exp}(3)$ RV to your histogram of `w`. Does it match? If $W \sim \text{Exp}(3)$, what is $\mathbb{E}[W]$?

::: answer
Not given
:::

### 2. Smoking policy and education

Let $X=$ highest education level and $Y=$ policy favored, from the table of 300 adults.

#### Part a

Make a table for the joint pmf $p_{X,Y}(x,y)$.

::: answer
Not given
:::

#### Part b

Find the marginal pmf $p_{X}(x)$.

::: answer
$p_X(\text{college}) = 0.25$, $p_X(\text{high school}) = 0.50$, $p_X(\text{grade school}) = 0.25$
:::

#### Part c

Find the marginal pmf $p_{Y}(y)$.

::: answer
Not given
:::

#### Part d

Make a table for the conditional pmf $p_{X|Y}(x|y)$.

::: answer
Partial answer: $p_{X|Y}(\text{high school} \mid \text{no smoking at all}) = \dfrac{30}{63} \approx 0.476$
:::

#### Part e

Make a table for the conditional pmf $p_{Y|X}(y|x)$.

::: answer
Partial answer: $p_{Y|X}(\text{no smoking at all} \mid \text{high school}) = \dfrac{30}{150} = 0.200$
:::

#### Part f

Are $X$ and $Y$ independent? Explain using your answers above.

::: answer
No. For example, $p_{X,Y}(\text{college}, \text{no restrictions}) = \frac{5}{300} \approx 0.017$, but $p_X(\text{college})\,p_Y(\text{no restrictions}) = 0.25 \times \frac{35}{300} \approx 0.029$.
:::

#### Part g

Simulate 10,000 adults by drawing from the table, to check one value from each of Parts a, d, and f.

::: answer
```{r}
#| label: "q2g-simulate"

set.seed(6969)
reps <- 10000

smoking_cells <- tibble(
  education = rep(c("College", "High school", "Grade school"),
                  each = 4),
  policy = rep(c("No restrictions", "Designated areas",
                 "No smoking", "No opinion"), times = 3),
  count = c(5, 44, 23, 3,
            15, 100, 30, 5,
            15, 40, 10, 10)
)

smoking_sims <- smoking_cells |>
  slice_sample(n = reps, weight_by = count, replace = TRUE)

smoking_summary <- smoking_sims |>
  summarise(joint = mean(education == "College" & policy == "No restrictions"),
            product = mean(education == "College") * mean(policy == "No restrictions"))

smoking_cond <- smoking_sims |>
  filter(policy == "No smoking") |>
  summarise(prob = mean(education == "High school"))
```

-   Joint $\approx$ `r round(smoking_summary$joint, 4)` and product $\approx$ `r round(smoking_summary$product, 4)`
-   $p_{X|Y}(\text{high school} \mid \text{no smoking at all}) \approx$ `r round(smoking_cond$prob, 4)`

Answers will vary slightly, but should be close to your answers in Parts a, d, and f.
:::

### 3. Expected value from a joint pdf

Consider the joint density $f_{X,Y}(x,y)= \dfrac32 x y$ for $0 \leq x$, $0 \leq y$, and $x+y \leq 2$.

#### Part a

Draw the possible values of $(X, Y)$.

::: answer
Not given
:::

#### Part b

Use 2D grid sampling to approximate $\mathbb{E}[X]$ and $\mathbb{E}[Y]$.

::: answer
```{r}
#| label: "q3b-simulate"

set.seed(7878)
reps <- 10000

triangle_grid <- expand_grid(x = seq(0, 2, length.out = 1001),
                             y = seq(0, 2, length.out = 1001)) |>
  filter(x + y <= 2) |>
  mutate(height = 3/2 * x * y)

triangle_sims <- triangle_grid |>
  slice_sample(n = reps, weight_by = height, replace = TRUE)

triangle_summary <- triangle_sims |>
  summarise(avg_X = mean(x), avg_Y = mean(y))
```

$\mathbb{E}[X] \approx$ `r round(triangle_summary$avg_X, 3)` and $\mathbb{E}[Y] \approx$ `r round(triangle_summary$avg_Y, 3)`

Answers will vary slightly, but should both be close to $\frac45 = 0.8$.
:::

#### Part c

Are $X$ and $Y$ independent? Explain, then check with your simulated pairs from Part b.

::: answer
```{r}
#| label: "q3c-check"

triangle_check <- triangle_sims |>
  summarise(joint = mean(x <= 1 & y <= 1),
            product = mean(x <= 1) * mean(y <= 1))
```

No. The possible values are a triangle, not a rectangle: the possible values of $Y$ ($0 \leq y \leq 2 - x$) depend on $x$. In the simulation, joint $\approx$ `r round(triangle_check$joint, 3)` but product $\approx$ `r round(triangle_check$product, 3)`.
:::

::: answer
The height is 2 (the rectangle's area is $\frac12$), and $0 \leq Z \leq 2$
:::

::: answer
Not given
:::

#### Part c

Simulate 10,000 pairs $(X, Y)$ to check your answer to Part b, and make a histogram of $Z$.

::: answer
```{r}
#| label: "q4c-simulate"
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3.5

set.seed(9898)
reps <- 10000

ratio_sims <- tibble(sim = 1:reps) |>
  mutate(x = runif(n(), min = 0, max = 1),
         y = runif(n(), min = 0.5, max = 1),

ggplot(ratio_sims, aes(x = z)) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

The simulated $P(Z \leq 1)$ should be close to your answer in Part b.
:::

### 5. Maude's phone and breakfast

Let $X$ be the number of days until Maude first loses her cell phone (1% chance each day), and $Y$ the number of days until she first forgets to eat breakfast (3% chance each day). $X$ and $Y$ are independent.

#### Part a

Find the joint pmf of $X$ and $Y$.

::: answer
$p_{X,Y}(x,y) = \left[0.99^{x-1}(0.01)\right]\left[0.97^{y-1}(0.03)\right]$ for $x = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$ and $y = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$
:::

#### Part b

Find the joint CDF of $X$ and $Y$ and briefly explain what $F_{X,Y}(x,y)$ represents.

::: answer
Not given
:::

#### Part c

Find the conditional pmf $p_{Y|X}(y|x)$.

::: answer
$p_{Y|X}(y|x) = 0.97^{y-1}(0.03)$ for $y = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$ (the same as $p_Y(y)$, since $X$ and $Y$ are independent)
:::

#### Part d

Find $F_{X,Y}(30, 10)$, then simulate 10,000 pairs of $(X, Y)$ to check your answer.

::: answer
```{r}
#| label: "q5d-simulate"

set.seed(2424)
reps <- 10000

maude_sims <- tibble(sim = 1:reps) |>
  mutate(X = rgeom(n(), prob = 0.01) + 1,
         Y = rgeom(n(), prob = 0.03) + 1)

prob_maude <- mean(maude_sims$X <= 30 & maude_sims$Y <= 10)
```

-   Exact: $F_{X,Y}(30, 10) \approx 0.0683$
-   Simulated: $\approx$ `r round(prob_maude, 4)`

Answers will vary slightly, but should be close to 0.0683.
:::

### 6. Minimum of a uniform and an exponential

$X$ and $Y$ are independent with $f_X(x)=\frac{1}{5}$ for $0\leq x\leq 5$ and $f_Y(y)=2e^{-2y}$ for $y>0$, and $Z = \min(X, Y)$.

#### Part a

Find the joint pdf $f_{X,Y}(x,y)$.

::: answer
Not given
:::

#### Part b

What are the possible values of $Z$? Find $P(Z > 0.5)$ exactly.

::: answer
$0 \leq Z \leq 5$, and $P(Z > 0.5) = P(X > 0.5)\,P(Y > 0.5) = \dfrac{4.5}{5}e^{-1} \approx 0.3311$
:::

#### Part c

Find the CDF of $Z$ for $0 \leq z \leq 5$.

::: answer
Not given
:::

#### Part d

Simulate 10,000 pairs of $(X, Y)$ to approximate $P(X < Y)$ and to check your answers to Parts b and c.

::: answer
```{r}
#| label: "q6d-simulate"

set.seed(3535)
reps <- 10000

min_sims <- tibble(sim = 1:reps) |>
  mutate(x = runif(n(), min = 0, max = 5),
         y = rexp(n(), rate = 2),
         z = pmin(x, y))

min_summary <- min_sims |>
  summarise(prob_x_less = mean(x < y),
            prob_z_big = mean(z > 0.5))
```

-   $P(X < Y) \approx$ `r round(min_summary$prob_x_less, 4)`
-   $P(Z > 0.5) \approx$ `r round(min_summary$prob_z_big, 4)`

Answers will vary slightly, but should be close to your answers in Parts b and c.
:::

### 7. Constant density on a quadrilateral

$X$ and $Y$ have constant joint density on the quadrilateral with vertices $(0,0)$, $(2,0)$, $(2,6)$, $(0,12)$.

#### Part a

For $0 \leq y \leq 6$, find the conditional density $f_{X|Y}(x|y)$.

::: answer
$f_{X|Y}(x|y) = \dfrac{1}{2}$ for $0 \leq x \leq 2$
:::

#### Part b

For $6 \leq y \leq 12$, find the conditional density $f_{X|Y}(x|y)$.

::: answer
Not given
:::

#### Part c

Find $P(0.5 \leq X \leq 3 \mid Y=7)$.

::: answer
$0.7$
:::

#### Part d

Simulate 10,000 values of $X$ given $Y = 7$ to check your answer to Part c.

::: answer
```{r}
#| label: "q7d-simulate"

set.seed(4646)
reps <- 10000
x_grid <- seq(0, 2, length.out = 10001)

slice_sims <- tibble(sim = 1:reps) |>
  mutate(x = sample(x_grid, size = n(), replace = TRUE,
                    prob = if_else(7 <= 12 - 3 * x_grid, 1/18, 0)))

prob_slice <- mean(slice_sims$x >= 0.5 & slice_sims$x <= 3)
```

$P(0.5 \leq X \leq 3 \mid Y=7) \approx$ `r round(prob_slice, 4)`

Answers will vary slightly, but should be close to 0.7.
:::

Find the CDF of $Z$ for $0 \leq z \leq 5$.

::: answer
Not given
:::

#### Part d

Simulate 10,000 pairs of $(X, Y)$ to approximate $P(X < Y)$ and to check your answers to Parts b and c.

::: answer
```{r}
#| label: "q6d-simulate"

set.seed(3535)
reps <- 10000

min_sims <- tibble(sim = 1:reps) |>
  mutate(x = runif(n(), min = 0, max = 5),
         y = rexp(n(), rate = 2),
         z = pmin(x, y))

min_summary <- min_sims |>
  summarise(prob_x_less = mean(x < y),
            prob_z_big = mean(z > 0.5))
```

-   $P(X < Y) \approx$ `r round(min_summary$prob_x_less, 4)`
-   $P(Z > 0.5) \approx$ `r round(min_summary$prob_z_big, 4)`

Answers will vary slightly, but should be close to your answers in Parts b and c.

### 7. Constant density on a quadrilateral

$X$ and $Y$ have constant joint density on the quadrilateral with vertices $(0,0)$, $(2,0)$, $(2,6)$, $(0,12)$.

#### Part a

For $0 \leq y \leq 6$, find the conditional density $f_{X|Y}(x|y)$.

::: answer
$f_{X|Y}(x|y) = \dfrac{1}{2}$ for $0 \leq x \leq 2$
:::

#### Part b

For $6 \leq y \leq 12$, find the conditional density $f_{X|Y}(x|y)$.

::: answer
Not given
:::

#### Part c

Find $P(0.5 \leq X \leq 3 \mid Y=7)$.

::: answer
$0.7$
:::

#### Part d

Simulate 10,000 values of $X$ given $Y = 7$ to check your answer to Part c.

::: answer
```{r}
#| label: "q7d-simulate"

set.seed(4646)
reps <- 10000
x_grid <- seq(0, 2, length.out = 10001)

slice_sims <- tibble(sim = 1:reps) |>
  mutate(x = sample(x_grid, size = n(), replace = TRUE,
                    prob = if_else(7 <= 12 - 3 * x_grid, 1/18, 0)))

prob_slice <- mean(slice_sims$x >= 0.5 & slice_sims$x <= 3)
```

$P(0.5 \leq X \leq 3 \mid Y=7) \approx$ `r round(prob_slice, 4)`

Answers will vary slightly, but should be close to 0.7.
:::
